root_cause.text: Holding req_lock while flushing rx_wq in nci_close_device creates a circular lock dependency because nci_rx_work running on rx_wq can call nci_request which reacquires req_lock.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and patch description explicitly state: "nci_close_device() flushes rx_wq and tx_wq while holding req_lock. This causes a circular locking dependency because nci_rx_work() running on rx_wq can end up taking req_lock too" and the patch moves the flush of rx_wq after releasing req_lock.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove flush of RX workqueue in nci_close_device to avoid deadlock when holding a lock, and update comment accordingly.
intent_record.what: Removed flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq) and updated comment in nci_close_device to note that RX workqueue flush cannot be done under the lock.
intent_record.how: The function no longer flushes the RX workqueue, preventing potential deadlock when holding a lock during device close; only the TX workqueue is flushed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Correct inaccuracies in comments about workqueue state and flush operation.
intent_record.what: Updated two comments: first comment now notes that rx work may be running (but will see NCI_UP cleared) instead of saying no works are scheduled; second comment now says 'Flush cmd and tx wq' instead of 'Flush cmd wq'.
intent_record.how: No functional change; only comment text was revised to better describe the state and operations at that point in the code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Flush rx workqueue after releasing req_lock to prevent use-after-free or race conditions during device close.
intent_record.what: Added a call to flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq) after mutex_unlock(&ndev->req_lock) in nci_close_device, along with a comment explaining that rx_work may take req_lock via nci_deactivate_target.
intent_record.how: Ensures that all pending work in the rx workqueue completes before the device close function returns, preventing potential use-after-free or race conditions that could occur if rx_work runs after the device resources are released.
